headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading error are plausible because Authelia can egress broadly while pdf.js processes PDF files in a browser-based worker model.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has broad network egress and B runs browsers on PDF files, so a malicious PDF could influence downstream handling if its content is manually or programmatically bridged into Authelia-related workflows. However, no shared channel or default ingestion path is documented, so the interaction is possible but not strongly evidenced.
conditions: IF PDF content from B is copied into an Authelia-managed workflow or admin console
IF an operator treats rendered PDF text as trusted instructions
mitigations: Keep PDF outputs out of auth/admin workflows
Use copy-paste only for vetted excerpts
Add a manual provenance check before acting on PDF-derived text
Separate browser testing from identity-management tasks
requires-engineering: add content provenance tagging between tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: B handles PDF documents and runs browsers, while A has broad network egress and calls OAuth/OpenID-related APIs. If sensitive PDF content is introduced into A’s context, A can transmit it outward; the pair lacks any documented isolation or redaction mechanism, so leakage is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF sensitive content from PDF files is passed into Authelia-facing prompts, logs, or configuration
IF Authelia forwards that content through its network egress or API calls
mitigations: Do not place secrets in PDFs processed by B
Redact PDFs before any handoff to A
Restrict A to non-sensitive test data
Review outbound requests from A for payload contents
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction at the handoff boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has broad network egress but no subprocesses, while B has browser execution and supports multiple instances. Their write surfaces do not overlap in the profiles, so direct resource contention is limited; uncertainty remains because shared filesystem or lock behavior is not documented.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external resource through network APIs
IF an orchestrator shares a writable workspace not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Avoid shared mutable targets
Run each agent in separate workspaces
Serialize any shared-resource updates
Check for hidden shared mounts before deployment
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: B processes PDF files in a browser-based worker model, and A can emit networked outputs via OAuth/OpenID-related APIs. If B consumes A-generated text or metadata without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions or rendered documents. The profiles do not show a verification gate, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF B treats A’s output as authoritative input
IF A-generated claims are rendered or acted on without a verification step
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before B uses them
Add a validation step for A-produced facts
Limit B to rendering only trusted sources
Log and diff A outputs before downstream use
requires-engineering: implement structured verification between agents

E_compliance.rationale: A is an identity/authentication component with broad egress, while B processes PDF documents locally with no network egress. No explicit residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to policy gaps if sensitive PDFs are routed through A; the other agent is not independently implicated.
conditions: IF regulated data from PDFs is routed through Authelia-managed services
IF organizational policy forbids identity-layer handling of that data class
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Document data-flow boundaries
Confirm retention settings for A
Use local-only PDFs for B
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
